reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is an instructional walkthrough of Coinbase versus Base self-custody, including wallet setup and use. The recovery-phrase interaction is accompanied by warnings to store the phrase securely and never share it, and the material does not show disclosure to another party or resulting asset movement. The rewards banner and referral links are described as ordinary contextual features without evidence of deceptive behavior, guaranteed returns, an unsafe destination, or a connection to the recovery-phrase handling.

citations.quote: I'm gonna walk you through how to download and set up this Coinbase wallet step-by-step
if you do want to download Coinbase while you're at it and get that free Bitcoin bonus, make sure you use my link down below
Some of the links on this webpage are affiliate links
save these 12 words in a secure location such as a password manager and never share them with anyone

opening.argument: The video ties an apparently free asset directly to a viewer action: it tells viewers to use the presenter’s link while offering a “free Bitcoin bonus.” The description reinforces that this is not merely educational material by labeling the link “Invest With Coinbase (Free Bitcoin!),” while the disclosure says the creator may earn a commission when viewers click and purchase or subscribe. That is a solicitation structure: click the external link, potentially take the required financial action, and receive the promised reward. The video also lists multiple other crypto or stock bonuses, broadening the same acquisition pattern across several destinations.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a walkthrough does not answer the concrete reward solicitation. The defense’s own cited material contains the instruction to use the presenter’s link for free Bitcoin, and the affiliate disclosure confirms a commercial incentive tied to clicking and potentially purchasing or subscribing. The absence of proof that every viewer received a reward does not negate the advertised action-reward pairing.

citations.quote: get that free Bitcoin bonus, make sure you use my link down below
we may earn a commission if you click through and make a purchase and/or subscribe

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited promotion does not establish that the bonus is fabricated, guaranteed, or obtained without ordinary eligibility conditions. The affiliate disclosure openly states that commissions may arise from clicks, purchases, or subscriptions, which is ordinary commercial disclosure rather than proof of deception. The tutorial’s core subject remains wallet setup and operation, including explicit warnings about the recovery phrase.

I'm gonna walk you through how to download and set up this Coinbase wallet step-by-step

opening.argument: The presentation places a concrete annual return claim inside a crypto wallet and conditions it on adding an asset. The wallet screen visibly says “Earn 4.1% rewards” and “Add USDC on Base to your wallet to earn 4.1% rewards per year.” That is a passive-return invitation attached to putting funds into the wallet, not merely a neutral explanation of wallet mechanics. The surrounding demonstration also shows a $50 Ethereum purchase and later a balance divided between Ethereum and Aerodrome Finance, reinforcing a pattern of moving assets into the app and then pursuing yield-like or token-related opportunities. A careful viewer could reasonably read the prominent reward banner as an inducement to fund participation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the rewards banner as an incidental feature, but it does not explain why the screen prominently links a yearly percentage to adding USDC. Nor does the instructional framing remove the financial inducement: the demonstrated workflow proceeds from buying Ethereum to holding and swapping crypto. The relevant concern is the combination of a stated annual reward and an asset-funding condition, not whether the presenter proves a loss on camera.

citations.quote: I'm just going to purchase $50 worth of Ethereum

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A banner displaying a percentage does not by itself establish a deceptive fixed or guaranteed return, and the video does not tell viewers that the reward is risk-free or that participation will profit them. The cited purchase and swap are demonstrations of wallet functions, while the presenter expressly identifies the content as not personalized financial advice. The return claim is therefore insufficient to convert the operational demonstration into a fraudulent investment offer.

citations.quote: I am not a financial advisor, and this isn't any kind of personalized financial advice
We have $40 dollars so if we click here on the two at the bottom, we can now see all of these different assets we can swap into

opening.argument: Although presented as education, the video repeatedly directs viewers toward buying and swapping specific crypto assets and toward commercial links. It demonstrates purchasing $50 of Ethereum, then proposes taking $20 of that balance and swapping it into Aerodrome, described as a popular altcoin. The description simultaneously advertises multiple exchange offers and affiliate destinations. This combination makes the tutorial function as a participation funnel: learn the wallet, fund it, then buy or swap tokens through linked services. The disclaimer does not remove the promotional effect of showing a concrete purchase-and-token pathway while inviting viewers to use monetized links.

Aerodrome, that's a popular altcoin
Some of the links on this webpage are affiliate links, meaning, at no additional cost to you, we may earn a commission if you click through and make a purchase and/or subscribe.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense’s educational label overlooks the actual calls to participate. The video does not stop at explaining custody: it walks through buying Ethereum and swapping part of the balance into a named altcoin, while the description supplies monetized links to exchanges and bonuses. Calling those links contextual does not change that viewers are directed toward purchases and token activity through them.

citations.quote: I'm just going to purchase $50 worth of Ethereum
we want to take $20 and swap it into Aero on base
we may earn a commission if you click through and make a purchase and/or subscribe

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The demonstrations show how the app operates, not a claim that Ethereum or Aerodrome will appreciate, pay dividends, or produce a return. The presenter even says the swap is for demonstration purposes, and the material explains fees, networks, custody, and recovery risks. Affiliate links and a tutorial can coexist without proving that token purchase is being misrepresented as profitable.
